item.title: This women led hub is reshaping climate justice discourse in Nigeria
item.description: Women Initiative for Sustainable Environment (WISE), a legally registered nonprofit organization that advances grassroots women’s representation, active participation, and leadership in natural resource governance and peace building.

item.title: Karnataka’s 2025 Devadasi Abolition Bill and the struggle for dignity in India
item.description: The Karnataka Devadasi Bill, 2025 aims to “conscientize” the public on the issue of getting girls and women dedicated as devadasis by subjecting to liberation from all hues of exploitation.

item.title: In Russia's Bashkiria region, a revived tradition of samovar dance parties for young people
item.description: A new season of “Samauryly Ritaiym” — the “samovar dances” — has kicked off in Bashkortostan. These vibrant events draw thousands of participants.

item.title: Jamaican bobsledders bring unexpected joy to an island beset with post-hurricane stress
item.description: The idea for the bobsled team, which gained fame through 1993’s “Cool Runnings,” had its origins in an annual push-cart derby, where homemade vending carts are used in competitive races.

item.title: Similar type of bot attacks target Instagram profiles of Serbian student movement and Macedonian independent media outlet
item.description: Large-scale bot operations targeted critical voices in Serbia and North Macedonia, attempting to trigger platform shutdowns and restrict public communication.

item.title: Water pollution in DRC attributed to Chinese mining company
item.description: While areas rich in rare minerals may be a blessing for the country’s economy, they can also be a curse for the local populations in the DRC.

item.title: Nigerian Muslim and Christian peace advocates call for calm, unity amid US designation as a ‘Country of Particular Concern’
item.description: “For decades, Nigerians have lived side by side in peace. Our unity is our strength, allowing foreign interests to divide us would be the greatest tragedy of all.”

item.title: When dreams meet digital recruitment scams: Bangladeshi workers in crisis
item.description: Bangladeshi migrant workers face rising digital scams exploiting limited digital literacy, informal brokers, and weak coordination among government agencies, leaving thousands stranded and in debt annually.

item.title: Samoa prime minister bans newspaper from attending press briefings
item.description: “Banning an entire news organization from press conferences hurts the public interest as people will lose access to independent reporting on matters of national importance.”

item.title: Critics say Hong Kong fire was due to negligence, not scaffolding
item.description: What we need includes an independent investigation into the malpractice surrounding repair project bidding, the failure of the current monitoring system and the inaction of government authorities upon receiving complaints.
